expected_symptom: internal_failure: llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type! (or its Debug-trap/HRESULT equivalents) when compiling repro.hlsl -T ps_6_0; fixed means this predicate stops matching, whether by a clean compile or by a comprehensible replacement diagnostic
history: always-repro'd v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (wording changed twice: access-violation -> DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR HRESULT -> plain E_FAIL text; never fixed)
reviewed_by: gpt-5.3-codex (independent batch-019 step-10 review; applied selectively at collation)
summary: Repros on main (89e2f98e2) and every stable release v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607, always. The diagnostic text drifts three times (access-violation crash on the oldest releases, a dedicated DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR HRESULT with an Internal Compiler error prefix on v1.6.2106-v1.6.2112, plain E_FAIL error: text from v1.7.2207 onward matching the reporter's exact 2023 quote) but none of the rewordings is the requested uninitialized-value diagnostic. Control with the index initialized compiles cleanly, isolating the defect to the uninitialized read rather than structured-buffer array-member codegen generally. CE (dxc_1_6_2112, dxc_trunk) corroborates with the Linux cast<X>() spelling.
title: Nonsensical error message when using undef offset in structured buffer
